fgos coordination run: missing --file is a validation error (exit 4)

fgos coordination run: a request file that does not exist is a validation error (exit 4)
fgos coordination run: a request file violating R2 (top-level executor field) is a validation error (exit 4) end to end through the real CLI

fgos coordination run --file <agent-led> genuinely dispatches through the real engine and closes the session; fgos coordination show reports it, read-only
fgos coordination run --file <declared consult>: dispatches both declared operations through the real engine and closes the session

fgos coordination run --cwd <worktree>: session/Assignment storage is governed by repoRoot (--dir), never relocated by --cwd (Phase 01 R8); ctx.cwd genuinely threads to the dispatched worker's own subprocess cwd instead, proven by a real marker file the worker writes into its own process.cwd()

fgos coordination show --cwd <anything>: repoRoot (--dir), never --cwd, governs which session is read -- a session opened at the repo root reads identically whether --cwd names a real linked worktree, an unrelated directory, or is omitted entirely (Phase 01 R8: --cwd has zero storage/read-location effect)
fgos coordination run --file <request> with --cwd OMITTED behaves byte-identically to today: the session lands under the repo root's own .fgos/

fgos coordination run --file <declared operation step, mutation:"mutating", result.kind:"work-product">, --cwd <linked worktree>: the request's mutation field reaches dispatchDeclaredOperation, so a real work-product mutation grades done/verified instead of being fail-closed by the read-only gate, and the persisted Assignment record itself carries mutation:"mutating"

fgos coordination run --file <declared operation step, mutation:"mutating", on an advisory operation>: refused by name through the CLI door -- an operation must declare result.kind:"work-product" before it may opt into a real, mutating dispatch
fgos coordination chain <track>: lists cells reconstructed from real sessions, names activeCell and nextAction for the still-open one
fgos coordination chain <track> on a track with zero matching sessions is a validation-free empty result, not an error
fgos coordination chain requires a track argument
R5: every place that enumerates the coordination sub-verb list (help text, error messages, the registry description) names "chain"

approve of a leaf whose root has NOT moved: no catchup attempted at all, unchanged from before this item (regression guard)

approve of a leaf whose root branch was never created (root only ever driven by a live session/pick, never the runner dispatch loop that creates fgw/<rootId> early per D17): falls back to creating it from main instead of crashing raw on the ancestor-check
approve of a leaf whose inline catchup hits a real conflict: parks blocked (reason merge-conflict), the leaf stays awaiting-approval-shaped (not silently delivered), root untouched
approve of a runner item that conflicts: aborts the merge, awaiting-approval -> blocked (reason merge-conflict), main left byte-for-byte unchanged (must_have: main never holds a broken merge commit)
approve of a runner item whose staged merge fails its own verify: aborts, awaiting-approval -> blocked (reason verify-fail-post-merge), main left unchanged
approve of a root item that HAD children, whose merge into main conflicts, parks with the distinguishing reason integration-drift and a main@<sha> friction detail
approve of a pull-door item (no merge, code already on main): re-verifies and closes awaiting-approval -> done with role human
approve of a legacy item with a failing verify: blocked (reason verify-fail), not merge-related, exit 0
approve verify-fail (legacy item): park edge stamps role 'system' (not human) on the awaiting-approval -> blocked event
approve of a legacy item with a passing verify closes it to done — legacy degrade never blocks approve/reject from working (must_have)
approve catches transitionWork CAS conflict when item becomes blocked before failure block write, returning structured result (AC4)
approve CAS conflict returns fresh actual status from store on event-regression replay / stale status (AC5)
approve --timeout and --no-timeout together are rejected as validation, exit 4
approve twice: the second approve on an already-done item is rejected as precondition, exit 2 (done is terminal)

approve --acknowledge-iron-law false (a value form, not the bare flag) still REFUSES -- fail-closed, review-20260718-self-improve-loop f02
approve of the same self-modifying diff PROCEEDS with --acknowledge-iron-law: merges, verifies, awaiting-approval -> delivered, branch SURVIVES (tsk-1p9: cleanup deferred to the cleanup verb)
approve of an ordinary runner item (diff touches no self-modifying module) is UNAFFECTED — proceeds to done with no --acknowledge-iron-law flag (backward compatibility)
approve of a leaf item forked AFTER a sibling already merged a gated-module change into the root does NOT trip Iron Law on the ancestor's file (tsk-4voj false-positive closed)
approve of a leaf item whose OWN commit touches a gated module (src/runner/**) PROCEEDS — the leaf lands on fgw/<root>, never trunk (iron-law-gate-human-ux D1)
approve of a milestone blocks when a targeted item's root has unsynced drift, exit 4, item stays awaiting-approval
approve of a milestone succeeds with --acknowledge-drift despite a targeted item's root having unsynced drift
approve of a milestone with no drift on any target succeeds normally, unaffected by the guard
approve of an ordinary item with no targets is completely unaffected by the close-out guard (regression)

approve --github without --pr is a validation error, item stays proposed, and mergeGitHubPR is never called
approve --github --pr on an item with a missing-evidence acceptance clause is refused BEFORE the real GitHub merge: precondition, exit 2, mergeGitHubPR/gh is never called
approve --github with a dirty main tree is NOT blocked by the local dirty-tree gate and proceeds to the GitHub merge
approve --github --pr on a fake gh merge success transitions the item awaiting-approval -> delivered with role human
approve --github --pr on a fake gh merge failure transitions awaiting-approval -> blocked and records friction with the classified reason, layer, and gh detail
approve refuses from inside a registered session worktree (runner source) — no merge, item stays proposed, main HEAD unchanged, exit 4
approve refuses from inside a registered session worktree (pull source) — refuses before any goal-check, item stays proposed, exit 4

approve refuses from an ad-hoc worktree never created through "fgos session start" (pull source) — refuses before any goal-check, item stays proposed, exit 4
approve from the main checkout is unaffected by the ad-hoc-worktree guard — runner and pull both still close to done, exit 0
approve --github --pr refuses from an ad-hoc worktree never created through "fgos session start" — no gh call, no moveWork, item stays proposed, exit 4

approve --github --pr refuses from inside a registered session worktree, with the registry guard's friendlier session-naming message (same precedence as the local path) — no gh call, item stays proposed, exit 4
approve --github --pr on a runner item touching a self-modifying-capable module REFUSES without --acknowledge-iron-law -- no gh call, item stays proposed, exit 4 (f01)
approve --github --pr on the same self-modifying diff PROCEEDS with --acknowledge-iron-law: merges via the fake gh, awaiting-approval -> done (f01)
approve on a proposed item with a missing-evidence acceptance clause is refused the same way as move --to done: precondition, exit 2, item stays proposed, no event written

pick --id claims that specific item, role fixed to "session" — pick has no --role flag at all, unlike take

the gated fixture is a discoverable core protocol whose window and gated binding survive the real loader
POSITIVE: the full independent cohort settles, the window opens, and the gated synthesis is authorized and dispatched with the branch outputs granted
NEGATIVE pre-window: neither an empty cohort nor a partial one opens the window, and the synthesis is refused at authorization
NEGATIVE unlisted source: an operation outside opensAfter.operationRefs[] cannot satisfy the window, however legitimately it completed
NEGATIVE unlisted source (unstamped work under the source operation's own claim key): the reserved stamp is the only channel a window source reads
NEGATIVE foreign session: a fully-settled cohort in ANOTHER session opens nothing here, and its refs are refused as a grant
NEGATIVE failed source: a cohort member that ran and FAILED leaves the window shut, and replay reports the same "failed" reason
NEGATIVE missing source: a cohort member never dispatched at all leaves the window shut with reason "missing"
NEGATIVE unknown window: a contextAccess.visibilityWindowRef naming an undeclared window is rejected at load, and the runtime derivation refuses one too
NEGATIVE Workflow profile: this fixture's own window block and gated binding are both rejected under a Workflow profile
NEGATIVE terminal authorization: an operation-authorized event that lands after the session closed is neutralized by replay, even with the window wide open
CRASH/RESUME: a window-gated dispatch interrupted mid-registration self-heals to the SAME Assignment while the window is still open
CRASH/RESUME fails closed: if the crash also cost a cohort member its linked result, the retry is refused rather than resumed
DEGENERATE: a window whose opensAfter.operationRefs[] is EMPTY validates and is permanently open, gating nothing
SCOPE BOUNDARY: a required binding carrying contextAccess.visibilityWindowRef validates but is NOT gated at dispatch (the gate lives on the grant door)
REPLAY PARITY: an independent replay of the real fixture reaches the same legality decision the live dispatch path reached, open and closed

R3: divergent-exploration branches (explorer-a/b/c) have NO topology edge among themselves -- every edge touching an explorer actor originates ONLY from facilitator-actor, so no branch can read a sibling's output before the declared cluster/fan-in point

R3: cluster-deduplicate, convergent-synthesis, and recommend-with-dissent (the three fan-in-style phases) have NO incoming topology edge at all -- fan-in is never expressed as a single privileged upstream "read" edge

R3: every declared topology edge caps maxRounds at exactly 1 -- no edge anywhere in this framework permits more than one round, structurally ruling out an unbounded back-and-forth dialogue on any edge
R3: cohort declares isolated-until-fan-in independence and the explorer role as a hard requirement, with no cohort.count mismatch trap (omitted, matching the already-documented planCohort fix)

R3: vote-as-truth / majority-based evidence confidence has no expressible field anywhere in this schema -- injecting a voting/consensus field at cohort, topology-edge, or operation scope is rejected by the REAL validateFlowDefinition
R3: recursive task graph / dynamic subgraph spawning has no expressible field -- injecting a spawn-shaped field on a graph node is rejected by the REAL validateFlowDefinition

R4: a real SECOND `fgos coordination run` invocation against the SAME coordinationId continues the session -- no duplicate Assignment, no reconsumed invocationKey, no lost disposition, no hidden-context leakage

R5 (resume-specific): once a session reaches a terminal status, a further CLI invocation naming the SAME coordinationId is refused -- terminal statuses stay absorbing across the resume door too, not just at open
the live request without its authorize steps cannot reach the revision or recheck operations at all
no observe door binds a name that could write, anywhere on its import path
show-run finds a run by its id and reports what is on disk
a run with no pane still reads cleanly -- visibility is optional, not missing
a corrupt visibility file degrades to a stated error instead of taking the reading down
an unknown run id says so rather than returning an empty reading
watch follows a run driven by somebody else and stops when that run stops
a watcher that runs out of ticks says so, rather than implying the run ended
an aborted watcher is distinguished from a finished run too
a run that reconciled to unknown is terminal for a watcher -- there is nothing more to see
reading a log or an outbox that does not exist yet is normal, not an error
recovery-planner.mjs imports no fs/adapter/network module and never reaches src/runner/coordination/
recover.mjs never reaches src/runner/coordination/ or any session/event-append binding -- no implicit close
plan() is pure and deterministic: same snapshot+evidence+intent -> same action/reason/evidenceIds/actionKey
replay parity: repeated observe calls against an unchanged run reproduce the same action/reason/evidenceIds
observe (no --action) is pure: never writes run.json or a recovery log, any number of calls
reassign without replacement-authority evidence gets a typed needs-input, never a silent default action
an outbox artifact of an unrecognized kind parks the recommendation instead of guessing an action
read and write paths derive identical legality for the same snapshot/evidence/action -- one shared evaluator, not two
apply refuses when any of the 5 required CAS fields is missing, typed
apply refuses as plan-stale when the run's observed snapshot changed since the recommendation was issued
two recommendations racing on the same starting state: the first apply wins, the second never repeats or corrupts its effect
apply refuses as plan-expired past the recommendation's own expiry
a repeat apply with an already-consumed action key returns the same prior outcome, never repeating the effect
a run directory already mid-apply refuses a second concurrent apply rather than corrupting state
F3: swapping the action under an unmatched actionKey is refused before ever reaching the legality check
read and write paths still derive identical legality for a genuinely matching action/actionKey pair
a schema-1 run.json with no controlEpoch field reads as epoch 0 and stays fully unaffected by an observe call
no implicit close: applying resume-driver never touches run.status or settles the run
applying resume-driver clears the assignment dispatch.claim after dead-driver recovery so retry can launch
checkApply is pure and agrees with the use case: same inputs, same outcome
H1: expectedControlEpoch reads run-lock's real generation ledger, never the run.json shadow field
H1: apply refuses via the live-holder gate when the observed epoch matches but a live controller still actively holds it
F1: a run that settles (result.json appears) between plan() and apply refuses as plan-stale even though run.json.status never changed
F5: a settle write landing exactly between acquireRunControl and the settled re-check is always caught, deterministically
F3: a valid actionKey from a different recommendation cannot be replayed against this one
M1: a stale .recovery.lock left by a dead process is reclaimed, not left stuck forever
M1: a .recovery.lock held by a live process is still refused, never reclaimed out from under it

approve (root-into-main merge): produces a diagnostic log record carrying mergedSha and mergedInto
approve (--github): produces a diagnostic log record carrying mergedSha and mergedInto
